instruction: Set Chrome's default font size to Large in the appearance settings.

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt install jq -y

mkdir -p /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && if [ ! -f /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences ]; then echo '{}' > /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences; fi && cd /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && jq '. + {"safebrowsing":{"enabled":false,"enhanced":false}}' Preferences > temp && mv temp Preferences

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent navigated Chrome menu -> Settings -> Privacy and Security -> Security. Found Safe Browsing section with Standard protection appearing selected. Model concluded it was already enabled and stopped without making changes. Evaluator returned 0 because safebrowsing was disabled in Preferences.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open Chrome three-dot menu, navigate to Settings, click Privacy and Security sidebar, navigate to Security subsection, read and understand settings options
metadata.failure_analysis: Model misread UI state - saw Standard protection radio button as selected but safe browsing was actually disabled via Preferences config. Did not click to toggle/enable the setting.
metadata.task_rationale: Tests a different Chrome settings change (font size via Appearance) using the same navigation capability the model demonstrated. Requires interacting with a dropdown control rather than a radio button, testing a different interaction pattern.
metadata.explanation: Task requires changing Chrome's default font size to Large (20px) in Appearance settings. Evaluator restarts Chrome and checks chrome_font_size preference using check_font_size metric, expecting value 20.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter 'chrome_font_size' correctly reads Chrome Preferences file at 'webkit.webprefs.default_font_size', which is the correct JSON path for Chrome's default font size setting.
Metric 'check_font_size' correctly extracts 'default_font_size' from the getter result dict and compares it against the expected value using equality check.
Expected value 20 correctly corresponds to Chrome's 'Large' font size option in the Appearance settings.
Postconfig correctly kills Chrome and restarts it to ensure the Preferences file is flushed to disk before the getter reads it.
The expected parameter handling is correct: get_rule returns {'type': 'value', 'value': 20}, and check_font_size accesses rule['type'] and rule['value'] directly.
Single-step instruction (set font size to Large) is fully covered by the single evaluator check.
